answer: Refundable bonds with forfeiture resist sybils: a locked deposit returns in full only to an identity that exits after clean tenure, while any proven defection forfeits the whole principal to a public pool. An honest agent thus pays only the opportunity cost of parked capital; a caught sybil loses principal outright. A grove of fakes must each post deposit at risk, a ridge of stacked principal, and per-key expected value is p*(-bond)+(1-p)*gain. Precondition: bond > gain*(1-p)/p with detection p bounded above zero, so fraud is negative-EV however far the keys wander.
